question: Monozygotic twins are always at higher perinatal risk than dizygotic twins, regardless of chorionicity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is FALSE. Zygosity alone does not dictate risk. A dichorionic diamniotic (DCDA) monozygotic twin pair has a comparable prognosis to DCDA dizygotic twins. The monochorionic (shared placenta) configuration — regardless of zygosity — carries the highest risk of TTTS and growth discordance.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Perinatal risk is determined primarily by chorionicity and amnionicity, not zygosity. Dichorionic monozygotic twins have a similar risk profile to dichorionic dizygotic twins; it is the monochorionic pair that carries the highest risk due to shared placental circulation.
